s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Tachycardia with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Normal blood pressure on presentation
Elevated white blood cell count
Normal serum calcium
Abnormal ECG findings
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography
Left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography and normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT and elevated cardiac biomarkers

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and potential link to adrenal mass

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and abnormal ECG findings

shortlist.label: Catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Potential link to pheochromocytoma and elevated cardiac biomarkers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin, and abnormal ECG findings, combined with the presence of systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography and normal coronary arteries, is consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The left-adrenal heterogeneous mass could be an incidental finding or a contributing stressor.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: While the left-adrenal mass could suggest pheochromocytoma, the normal blood pressure on presentation and lack of other specific symptoms make this less likely.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This is essentially another term for Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, and the same reasoning applies.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While this could be a consideration with the adrenal mass, the specific pattern of apical ballooning and other findings point more directly to Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
